paragraphs: Rav Shisha (or Sheshet), son of Rav Idi bar Avin. Of his father, Rav Idi bar Avin, it is related in [Pesachim 49a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.49a.16) [supplied: פסחים מט.] that he married a kohen's daughter and she bore him two ordained sons [סמיכי], Rav Sheshet and Rav Yehoshua. Their father was a disciple of Rav Chisda, as explained in his entry. And Rav Shisha his son lived in the time of Abaye and Rava,

and he received [traditions] from his father, as in [Taanit 13a](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.13a.3-4): Abaye questions Rav Idi bar Avin, and Rav Shisha son of Rav Idi explains what his father found difficult.[^10] Hyman writes: And everywhere he is mentioned only by the name Rav Shisha son of Rav Idi, as in Berakhot 4a (according to the reading of דק״ס), 17a, [24a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.24a.3), [Shabbat 114b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.114b.4); Pesachim 49b;[^11] [54b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.54b.13), 115a, Rosh Hashanah 6b,[^16] [Moed Katan 11b](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.11b.3), Yevamot

[82a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.82a.4), [Ketubot 33a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.33a.8), [88a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.88a.2), [Bava Kamma 87a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.87a.2), [Bava Batra 102b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.102b.1); [Zevachim 14b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.14b.9). And sometimes he is mentioned by the name Rav Sheshet son of Rav Idi, as in [Shabbat 138b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.138b.2-3); [Eruvin 102a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.102a.18), [Pesachim 84b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.84b.10), Sukkah 53a,[^17] [Bava Metzia 6a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.6a.9), [65a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.65a.13), [109a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.109a.9), [Zevachim 6a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.6a.9-11), and Hyman reports that in almost all of these places דק״ס reads Rav Shisha. And we find in Shabbat 116b that he expounded in the name of R. Yochanan.[^12]

And in [Ketubot 19b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.19b.1) he said: 'Learn from this: מדר״ב [unresolved as supplied; the parallel in [Ketubot 19b:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.19b.1) reads “from Rav Kahana”], etc.' In [Moed Katan 14b](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.14b.4), one version names him as the one who transmits a ruling in Shmuel’s name. In [Rosh Hashanah 27a](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_Hashanah.27a.17), he transmits a teaching in Rav Shmuel bar Yitzchak’s name. And in [Yevamot 74b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.74b.17-18) he challenges the words of Rava, and Rava answered.[^13] And we likewise find that he engaged in give-and-take with ר״פ [read as Rav Papa from the following context], as in Bava Metzia

[65a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.65a.13), [109a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.109a.9): he raised an objection to Rav Papa, and called him 'Mar' [Master]. And in [Bava Batra 8a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.8a.6) Rav Papa spoke to him. And in Shabbat 146a Rav Papa said: Whatever is done for adornment is permitted, as in the case of Rav Shisha son of Rav Idi, who used to adorn himself with his sheet; Hyman infers from this that he died before Rav Papa.[^14] And in Menachot 21a Rav Mordechai said to Rav Ashi: Thus said Rav Shisha son of Rav

notes.text: Printed citation labels and their daf locators (colon/full stop) are retained literally in the English; no modern numbering verified against any supplied witness.
דק״ס is not in the frozen acronym registry; rendered 'Dikdukei Soferim' as an unverified conventional reading, flagged uncertain.
'מדר״ב' is unknown in the registry; the expansion 'Rav Beivai (?)' is uncertain and the Hebrew is the source. Likewise ר״פ is rendered Rav Papa from the following context ('אמר לו רב פפא').
The printed 'יז. כד.' and 'קטו.' lack masekhet; the masekhet shown is a contextual inference and unresolved.

The complete named Davidson Ketubot19b opening paragraph says Rav Sheshet son of Rav Idi, שמע מינה מדרב כהנא (“learn from Rav Kahana”). This is an exact source comparison for Hyman’s compressed ש״מ מדר״ב, not an admitted expansion of the final letter or proof of the printed reading. The supplied מדר״ב and Shisha/Sheshet variants remain visible; the old Beivai suggestion stays only in historical notes.

The saved Pesachim49a paragraph supports ordained sons, not close-in-age sons, and has Rabbi Yehoshua where Hyman writes Rav Yehoshua. Hyman’s inference from past-tense adornment to death before Rav Papa remains his inference, not newly established chronology.

Fresh named digital comparisons retain occurrence-specific Shisha/Sheshet forms. Taanit 13a has Idi’s statement, Abaye’s reply and Shisha’s explanation of his father’s difficulty. Ketubot 19b names Rav Sheshet son of Rav Idi and reads “from Rav Kahana”; supplied מדר״ב remains unresolved, with no admitted expansion or printed-letter repair. Moed Katan 14b offers Ameimar or, alternatively, Rav Shisha as transmitter of Shmuel’s statement; Rosh Hashanah 27a names Rav Shmuel bar Yitzchak. Yevamot 74b continues onto 75a for Rava’s response. Bava Metzia 65a has Sheshet addressing Rav Papa as Mar, whereas 109a has Shisha; Bava Batra 8a places Shisha’s question before Papa’s response. Positive comparisons for the supplied Shabbat 116b report occur in the fetched Shabbat 146b paragraph (expounding in Rabbi Yochanan’s name); the adornment report supplied as Shabbat 146a occurs in fetched 147a; Menachot supplied 21a has the named Mordechai–Ashi–Shisha chain in fetched 21b. These comparisons leave Hyman’s literal citations visible. His Dikdukei Soferim preferences, exhaustive-name wording, Rav Chisda discipleship and chronology remain attributed reports or inferences, not a fresh apparatus census, genealogy or identity admission. All existing notes and the source hold are retained.

Hyman’s printed notice (vol. III, p. 1116) gives מדר״ב in his abbreviated quotation of Ketubot 19b. The consulted Davidson text names Rav Sheshet son of Rav Idi and gives “from Rav Kahana.” The abbreviation is retained as printed. Hyman’s printed references to Shabbat 146b for the teaching in Rabbi Yochanan’s name and 147a for the sheet match the consulted passages. The supplied transcription has 116b and 146a. Hyman prints Menachot 21a, and the consulted Mordechai–Ashi–Shisha exchange is on 21b. His report of the Dikdukei Soferim name readings and his inference about the order of deaths remain his.

[Pesachim 49a:16](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.49a.16) and [Ketubot 19b:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.19b.1) read Rav Sheshet, while [Taanit 13a:3–4](https://www.sefaria.org/Taanit.13a.3-4) reads Rav Shisha when he explains his father’s question. [Moed Katan 14b:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.14b.4) offers Ameimar and Rav Shisha as alternate transmitters. [Seder HaDorot 3315](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3315&lang=en) discusses both spellings and cautiously suggests that they refer to the same person.

The family notice cited as 49b occurs at [Pesachim 49a:16](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.49a.16) in the consulted text, which names Sheshet. The consulted [Pesachim 54b:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.54b.13) gives Shisha son of Rav Idi. [Berakhot 24a:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.24a.3) also gives Shisha.

[Zevachim 6a:9-11](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.6a.9-11) has Sheshet in the first statement and Shisha when Rav Ashi restates his question. The public teaching in Rabbi Yochanan’s name is at [Shabbat 146b:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.146b.6), as in Hyman’s printed reference.
Rava’s reply begins on [Yevamot 74b:17-18](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.74b.17-18) and continues at [Yevamot 75a:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.75a.1).

The garment anecdote is at [Shabbat 147a:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.147a.8), as cited in the printed edition. The passage describes a past practice. The inference about when Shisha died is Hyman’s.
The statement Rav Mordechai relays to Rav Ashi occurs at [Menachot 21b:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Menachot.21b.13) in the consulted text.

[Rosh Hashanah 7b:16](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_Hashanah.7b.16) gives Shisha son of Rav Idi on why the Mishnah omits New Years that depend on an action. Hyman cites Rosh Hashanah 6b. The Dikdukei Soferim reading he reports at Berakhot 4a has not been independently collated.

[Sukkah 56a:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.56a.12) gives Sheshet son of Rav Idi on the order of the blessings. Hyman cites Sukkah 53a. The etrog discussion at [Sukkah 46b:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Sukkah.46b.13) separately gives Shisha.
